title: Patient Encounter Performance Rubric
instructions: Rate the student’s performance as supported by the encounter. Rate only what the scenario makes possible to observe; use N/A when a criterion is not appropriate.

descriptors.4: Introduces self and role; establishes purpose and agenda; confirms the patient’s immediate concern; sets expectations.
descriptors.3: Opens clearly and establishes a workable focus.
descriptors.2: Opening is understandable but misses role, agenda, or patient priorities.
descriptors.1: Begins abruptly, creates confusion, or lacks a clinically appropriate purpose.

descriptors.4: Uses attentive, nonjudgmental, culturally responsive language; acknowledges emotion and patient perspective; builds trust.
descriptors.3: Consistently respectful and responsive; patient appears heard.
descriptors.2: Generally respectful but responses feel formulaic, rushed, or insufficiently attuned.
descriptors.1: Dismissive, judgmental, confusing, or emotionally unsafe communication.

descriptors.4: Uses open questions, focused follow-up, clarification, and appropriate sequencing; explores relevant history, context, risks, and goals.
descriptors.3: Gathers most relevant information with logical follow-up.
descriptors.2: Gathers some relevant information but is incomplete, disorganized, or overly leading.
descriptors.1: Misses essential information or cannot sustain a useful history.

descriptors.4: Recognizes verbal cues, uncertainty, concerns, questions, and changes in the patient’s story; avoids interrupting or ignoring information.
descriptors.3: Tracks the patient’s narrative and follows up appropriately.
descriptors.2: Responds to obvious cues but overlooks subtler concerns or inconsistencies.
descriptors.1: Ignores, contradicts, or prematurely redirects important information.

descriptors.4: Explains findings or next steps clearly; checks understanding; invites questions; incorporates preferences and readiness when relevant.
descriptors.3: Provides clear, patient-centered explanations and checks understanding.
descriptors.2: Explanation is partly clear but uses jargon, gives limited rationale, or does not check understanding.
descriptors.1: Provides inaccurate, overly technical, coercive, or absent explanation when needed.

descriptors.4: Identifies important findings; distinguishes relevant from irrelevant information; recognizes red flags or uncertainty; forms a plausible assessment or differential when appropriate.
descriptors.3: Reasoning is clinically coherent and appropriately cautious.
descriptors.2: Recognizes some key findings but misses connections, alternatives, or uncertainty.
descriptors.1: Reasoning is unsupported, unsafe, internally inconsistent, or absent when required.

descriptors.4: Maintains boundaries; protects privacy; communicates limitations; summarizes; confirms next steps, follow-up, or escalation when relevant.
descriptors.3: Professional and safe throughout; closes with a clear shared plan.
descriptors.2: Mostly professional but closure, limitations, or safety-netting is incomplete.
descriptors.1: Creates safety risk, overstates certainty, breaches boundaries, or ends without an appropriate plan.

scoring.interpretation: Use the total as a discussion aid, not a pass/fail grade. A score of 1 in professionalism, safety, or clinical reasoning should trigger review even when the total is high.
